posting.headline: IT Manager (device management and daily tech fixes), Cairo
posting.about: KMSC runs the field operations that produce the data behind a new generation of artificial intelligence, at factories, warehouses, and farms across Cairo. Every device the company owns sits in one management tool, and you run it: enrolment, location, lost mode, and the daily tech fixes on the floor. You report to the CTO.
do: Enrol and label every new device before it goes to a site.
Check the device list against the devices on the ground every week: same tags, same sites, same number.
Keep location on for every device, and chase any that goes dark the same day.
Manage every device from your screen: apps, settings, and restarts.
Fix the daily tech problems of operators and the managers who run our sites, from your screen first and on site if you must.
Test every update on a few devices first, then roll it out to the fleet in stages.
need: You have managed a fleet of devices or computers for a company, with a management tool.
Careful with a list, so every device has a tag, a row, and a dot on the map.
Patient on a call with someone who is not technical and is in a hurry.
Reachable at any hour for a missing device, with lost mode within the hour, every time.
plus: You have rolled out software updates across a fleet in stages.
You have supported people in the field, not only at a desk.
offer: A steady monthly wage, paid on time.
One tool, one fleet, and one list that is yours to keep clean.
Every procedure written down: enrolment, the missing device, the update, and the count.
A direct line to the CTO, and a fleet that grows from hundreds of devices to thousands.
posting.apply: Send your name, where you live, a phone number, and the fleets or tools you have managed. We call back within two working days to book your onboarding screening.

offer.heading: Offer of employment
paragraphs: We are pleased to offer you the position of IT Manager at KMSC. You will report to {manager}, the CTO.
Your start date is {start}. In your first weeks you take over Hexnode, match the device list to the registry, and enrol your first batch of phones. {manager} checks your work.

handbook.purpose: The client pays for accepted hours, and every hour comes from a phone. Hexnode is how we see every phone, lock it, and control it from anywhere, including the ones at delivery partners. You run it. A phone off the map, a stale location, or a tech problem that stops someone filming is yours to fix the same day.
outcomes: Every phone the company owns shows on the map with its tag and its site.
The device list matches the registry every Thursday.
A missing phone is in lost mode within the hour.
No update reaches the fleet before the two test phones pass a full test shift.
daily: Morning. Open Hexnode. Every phone due online is online, with a position from the last 45 minutes. A phone dark since last night: call its Portfolio Manager.
All day. Tech problems from operators and Portfolio Managers: a login, an upload, a setting, a restart. From your screen first, the site if you must.
Same day. New phones from the Inventory Manager: enrol, label, lock the collection app as the only app, check the registry row. Hand them back for the test recording.
Same hour. A missing phone. Find it on the map, put it in lost mode, tell Moharam and its Portfolio Manager. Nobody wipes it yet.
After 24 hours. A phone still missing is wiped when Mazen tells you. Mark it lost in the device list.
Test phones. Check the two test phones for a new version of the collection app. A new version means a full test shift before the fleet gets it.
weekly: Thursday, before 4:00 PM. Clean the device list for the weekly count: every phone on the map, tag matching its registry row. Send Mazen the MDM number.
Once a week. The week's fixes with Youssif: what broke, what keeps breaking, what to change on the phones.
Once a week. The partner phones: every one on the map and sending a position. One gone dark goes to Moharam.
monthly: Month end. The month's app versions and settings with Youssif. Agree on what changes next month.
Month end. Retire what cannot be repaired: wipe it, remove it from Hexnode, and Mazen closes its row.
standards: Enrolled before it is tagged, tagged before it joins a kit. A phone we cannot see does not go to a site.
The collection app is the only app on the phone. Nobody installs anything but you.
Location tracking stays on: every 45 minutes, and live the moment a phone reconnects.
Lost mode within the hour. Wipe only after 24 hours, and only when Mazen or Moharam tells you.
Every update goes to the two test phones first, always. The fleet gets it after a full test shift passes.
The device list and the registry say the same number. Any gap is found the same day.
An app bug goes to Youssif, never to the client. Money to Ahmed Alaa, papers to Mano.
never: Never wipe first. Find it, lock it, wait 24 hours, then wipe. A wiped phone cannot be found.
Never send an update to the fleet before the two test phones pass a full test shift.
A phone that goes home, or an account that is shared, ends the job.
Saying the client's name or the app's name outside the company ends the job.

firstMonth.what: Hexnode with Youssif: every setting, the map, lost mode, the device list. The store with Mazen: the registry and the tags.
Match the device list to the registry, phone by phone. Take every tech call from operators and Portfolio Managers yourself.
Enrol one full batch of phones for a new site, and run one update through the two test phones. Youssif checks your work.
A Thursday count where the device list matches the registry, tag by tag. Youssif signs you off.

measures: Phones on the map with a position from the last 45 minutes, every day.
Minutes from a phone reported missing to lost mode. Under 60, every time.
Thursday counts where the device list matched the registry.
Tech problems fixed the same day, and the ones that came back.
handbook.call: Youssif, for Hexnode, an app bug, or anything you cannot fix. Mazen for the registry, the tags, and any phone that moves. Moharam for a missing phone and anything on the floor. Ahmed Alaa for money. Mano for papers. An injury or the police: Moharam, then Adham.
